name: Curiosity Philosophy Benchmark v1
purpose: Fixed topics for evaluating whether the loop deepens curiosity rather than drifting into generic philosopher comparison.
topics: Is curiosity a virtue, a method, or a danger to certainty?
Is wonder different from curiosity in the beginning of philosophy?
Can curiosity destroy certainty, or does it require certainty as fuel?
Is skepticism disciplined curiosity or the failure of curiosity?
Does inquiry require ignorance, or does it require prior knowledge?
When does intellectual curiosity become intellectual vice?
Is intellectual humility a form of curiosity or a limit placed on curiosity?
Can education preserve curiosity while teaching established knowledge?
Is the desire for truth separable from curiosity?
Can an AI be curious without desire?
What is the difference between curiosity as appetite and curiosity as method?
Is doubt an obstacle to inquiry or the condition that makes inquiry possible?
Does curiosity need a stopping rule to become knowledge?
Can excessive openness become epistemic weakness?
Is curiosity morally neutral, or does it need ethical discipline?
Does scientific inquiry depend more on curiosity or on method?
Is philosophical curiosity different from information-seeking?
Can curiosity be trained without becoming dogmatic?
Does curiosity aim at truth, novelty, or transformation of the inquirer?
What is the strongest objection to treating curiosity as an intellectual virtue?
